html:
French settlers sent by the Company of the American Islands landed on Guadeloupe in June 1635, the same year d'Esnambuc took Martinique. They fought the Kalinago for years and drove most of them off.

The settlers grew tobacco and then sugar, with enslaved Africans brought in growing numbers. Guadeloupe was smaller and poorer than Martinique, and for a time it was governed from there.

Britain took the island several times, most importantly in 1759. Apart from those years and a short Swedish claim in 1813, it has stayed French. Since 1946 it has been an overseas department.
